# Words with several senses

Each sense is its own entry. Take the default when the request gives no context. Ask the question only when the request leaves the sense open and the answer changes the notes; a batch run takes the stated option without asking.

## Senses

| Word | Senses | Default | Question |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| arabic | `scale.arabic.phrygian-dominant`: Arabic as a scale name means Phrygian dominant. One library gives the name arabian to Locrian major, which this entry does not take.<br>`scale.arabic.double-harmonic`: Very arabic or byzantine means double harmonic major, with its flat second and flat sixth. | `scale.arabic.phrygian-dominant` |  |
| bebop minor | `scale.bebop-minor.bebop-dorian`: Bebop minor can mean bebop Dorian, which adds a passing major third to Dorian.<br>`scale.bebop-minor.bebop-harmonic-minor`: Bebop minor can also mean bebop harmonic minor, which adds a passing major seventh to natural minor. | `scale.bebop-minor.bebop-dorian` | Does bebop minor mean bebop Dorian or bebop harmonic minor? When to ask: The request says bebop minor with no mode word. A batch run takes bebop Dorian. Batch default: `scale.bebop-minor.bebop-dorian`. |
| cinematic | `mood.cinematic.drama`: A cinematic request that means drama: natural minor. This is the batch default.<br>`mood.cinematic.wonder`: A cinematic request that means wonder: Lydian. | `mood.cinematic.drama` | Should cinematic sound like wonder (Lydian) or drama (natural minor)? When to ask: The request names no other mood or scale word. A batch run takes drama. Batch default: `mood.cinematic.drama`. |
| diminished | `scale.diminished.half-whole`: Diminished as a scale name means the half-whole set when a dominant chord is present.<br>`scale.diminished.whole-half`: Diminished over a diminished chord means the whole-half set. | `scale.diminished.half-whole` | Does diminished mean the half-whole or the whole-half scale? When to ask: The request gives no chord context. Over a dominant chord the half-whole set is taken without asking. Batch default: `scale.diminished.half-whole`. |

| gallop | `rhythm.gallop.forward`: Per beat, a long note then two short ones at +0, +0.5 and +0.75 beat, with lengths 0.5, 0.25 and 0.25. Staccato halves the lengths.<br>`rhythm.gallop.reverse`: The reverse gallop: per beat two short notes then a long one at +0, +0.25 and +0.5 beat. | `rhythm.gallop.forward` |  |
| gypsy | `scale.gypsy.minor`: Gypsy minor means Hungarian minor, and a plain gypsy request takes it.<br>`scale.gypsy.major`: Gypsy major means double harmonic major.<br>`scale.gypsy.spanish`: Spanish gypsy means Phrygian dominant. | `scale.gypsy.minor` |  |
| half-time | `position.half-time.snare-on-three`: The tempo stays and the snare or clap lands only on slot 8, beat 3. Kick sits on 0 with few extras, and hats and bass keep full-tempo density.<br>`position.half-time.halved-tempo`: The tempo itself is halved, so the whole pattern runs at half speed. | `position.half-time.snare-on-three` | Should half-time keep the tempo and move the snare to beat 3, or halve the tempo? When to ask: The request states a BPM. Batch default: `position.half-time.snare-on-three`. |
| in A | `key.in-a.major`: In A alone reads as A major by the standard. Dance requests often mean minor, so record the assumption or ask.<br>`key.in-a.minor`: In A can mean A minor, especially in a request for a minor dance genre. | `key.in-a.major` | Is in A the key of A major or A minor? When to ask: The request says in A with no mode word. A batch run takes minor in a minor genre, else major. Batch default: `key.in-a.major`. |
| octave label | `notation.octave-label.c3`: Some programs label note 60 C3, so the octave number is the note number divided by 12, rounded down, minus 2. Serum 2 labels it C3, and the Vital label is not checked yet. The Serum 2 guide also calls 440 Hz A4, which is the scientific name; in the C3 convention that note is A3, so the guide mixes the two and a probe of the app should settle it.<br>`notation.octave-label.c4`: Scientific pitch notation labels note 60 C4: the octave number is the note number divided by 12, rounded down, minus 1. Note 21 is A0 and note 127 is G9. It rests on search excerpts and is not checked against a full source.<br>`notation.octave-label.c5`: Some programs label note 60 C5, so the octave number is the note number divided by 12, rounded down. Note 21 is A1 and note 127 is G10. | `notation.octave-label.c4` | Which name does your program show for middle C (note 60): C3, C4 or C5? When to ask: A request gives a note name with an octave number. Batch default: `notation.octave-label.c4`. |
| offbeat | `position.offbeat.eighth`: The eighth-note 'and' between beats, where slot mod 4 is 2: slots 2, 6, 10 and 14.<br>`position.offbeat.sixteenth`: Any sixteenth that is off the beat, where slot mod 4 is 1 or 3. Producers say 'offbeat 16ths' for it.<br>`position.offbeat.psytrance`: In a psytrance bass line, notes sit after the kick and never on it: one on the 'and' or three after the kick. | `position.offbeat.eighth` | Does offbeat mean the eighth 'and', any off-beat sixteenth, or a psytrance bass line? When to ask: The request asks for a psytrance bass line. Every other request takes the eighth 'and'. Batch default: `position.offbeat.eighth`. |
| open | `voicing.open.voicing`: Tones spread out: some neighbours are five or more semitones apart, or the whole chord spans more than an octave. Either condition counts.<br>`voicing.open.fifths`: Tones stacked in fifths with no third, so the chord sounds hollow and wide. It is common in film writing.<br>`voicing.open.guitar-chord`: A chord shaped like a guitar open-string chord: four to six tones, none below the low open string at 40.<br>`position.open.hat`: An open hi-hat, played on the offbeat slots 2, 6, 10 and 14 as in house and trance. | `voicing.open.voicing` | Which open do you mean: an open voicing, open fifths, an open guitar chord or an open hi-hat? When to ask: The text names no voicing. A batch run takes the open voicing. Batch default: `voicing.open.voicing`. |
| pentatonic | `scale.pentatonic.minor`: Pentatonic alone means minor pentatonic in a minor genre and major pentatonic otherwise. | rolling | `bass.rolling.grid`: The psytrance and techno bass grid: kick on every beat and a bass note on each other sixteenth, 12 per bar on one pitch. Notes are equal in velocity, 0.125 to 0.19 beat long (gate 60) and never legato.<br>`bass.rolling.dnb`: In drum and bass, either a busy top loop under simple drums or a busy mid bass over a steady sub. See the named rhythm hat roll. | `bass.rolling.grid` | Is the rolling line a bass grid, a drum and bass bass line, or a hat roll? When to ask: The request asks for a drum and bass bass line. Every other request takes the bass grid. Batch default: `bass.rolling.grid`. |

| shell | `voicing.shell.root-3rd-7th`: Only the root, third and seventh of a seventh chord. The fifth is left out.<br>`voicing.shell.root-and-named`: For a triad, the root plus one named note such as the third or fifth. This is the second reading of the word. | `voicing.shell.root-3rd-7th` |  |
